LanguageData.VP_Preset_FaithfulDesc: Closest to unmodded RimWorld. Two to three traits, a vanilla passion budget, and a narrow skill spread.
LanguageData.VP_Preset_DistinctDesc: The mod's signature tuning. Pawns have strong individual strengths and weaknesses while maintaining a fair colony average.
LanguageData.VP_Preset_WildcardDesc: Maximum variation. Pawns can arrive with 0 to 8 traits, zero or many passions, and wide skill swings.
LanguageData.VP_Preset_DesperateDesc: Scraped together survivors. Low skills, few passions, and poor rolls are common.
LanguageData.VP_Preset_EliteDesc: Refined imperial nobility and high-born pawns. Consistently high capability and polished skills.
LanguageData.VP_Preset_SovereignDesc: Archite lords, Sanguophages, and supreme leaders. Top-tier skill growth and wide passions.
LanguageData.VP_Preset_SpecialistDesc: Engineered single-domain specialists (Genies, Hussars). Focused skill spikes with domain passions.
LanguageData.VP_Preset_ScavengerDesc: Wasteland survivors, pirates, and scavengers. Lower baseline skills with tough survival rolls.
LanguageData.VP_CustomProfileDesc: Editable custom profile. Adjust sliders below to customize pawn generation.
LanguageData.VP_Confirm_ResetProfile: Reset this profile to {0}? All of its current values will be replaced.
LanguageData.VP_Confirm_DeleteProfile: Delete the profile "{0}"? This cannot be undone.
LanguageData.VP_QualityTip:
Every pawn rolls a quality. That roll picks one point between the handles of each range below: 0 lands on the low handle, 1 on the high handle.

This slider sets the average. Individual pawns roll around it.

Trait count and Child shift stop there, because their handles are hard limits. Skill shift and Passion budget add their spread on top, so pawns can be carried past those handles.
LanguageData.VP_TypicalTip: The average pawn this profile generates, against the Faithful baseline (0.25).\n\nCounts starting skill levels and the passion budget only, not traits. It also says nothing about how much pawns differ from each other, so two profiles with the same figure can play very differently.
LanguageData.VP_BestOfNRow: Best of {0} rerolls: {1} vs Faithful ({2}) — what you actually get if you reroll for this profile
LanguageData.VP_BestOfNTip:
Generate {0} pawns and keep the best one.

Closer to how the game is actually played: you reroll starting colonists, choose which prisoners to recruit, and turn down quest pawns.

Two figures close together means a consistent profile. A steep climb between them means a gambling one, and it pays off when you get to choose.
LanguageData.VP_Fingerprint: Traits {0}–{1} · Passions {2}–{3} · Skill shift {4} to {5} · Quality {6}
LanguageData.VP_Section_SkillsTip: When off, this profile leaves vanilla skill levels untouched.
LanguageData.VP_SkillSpreadTip:
How far a single pawn's own skills spread apart from each other, in skill levels. This is the typical spread, not the maximum; the line below shows the extreme.

Drawn separately for every skill, so it makes one pawn uneven. It does not make pawns differ from each other, which is what the quality roll does.

It is added on top of Skill shift, so a high value can push individual skills past either handle of that range.
LanguageData.VP_SkillSpreadDerived: extreme ±{0} lv per skill · most skills land {1} – {2}
LanguageData.VP_SkillShiftTip:
Levels added to or taken from every skill, on top of the vanilla roll.

A TARGET, NOT A LIMIT. Quality picks one point between the handles: the low handle is what the lowest-quality pawn aims for, the high handle the highest. Skill spread then scatters that pawn's twelve skills around that point, and can carry them past either handle.

Set the handles for the pawn you expect. Set Skill spread for how far the exceptions stray.
LanguageData.VP_ChildShiftToggle: Also shift skills when a child grows up
LanguageData.VP_ChildShiftToggleTip:
Not recommended. Diverges from vanilla growth.

Vanilla never re-rolls skill levels at age 13. This shifts them at that growth moment, so colonists can gain or lose skill levels on their birthday.

Traits and passions at 13 are unaffected. Requires "Apply variance to children growing up" in General settings.
LanguageData.VP_ChildShiftTip:
Levels added to or taken from each skill at the age-13 growth moment.

A HARD LIMIT, unlike Skill shift above. Skill spread still varies each skill inside these handles, but no skill is carried past them.

The difference is deliberate. At generation the pawn's levels were just rolled, so straying costs nothing. At 13 they are twelve years of play, so a minimum of 0 has to genuinely mean "never takes levels away".
LanguageData.VP_ChildShiftCaptionSafe: The minimum is at or above zero, so growing up can never cost a pawn skill levels.
LanguageData.VP_ChildShiftCaptionLossy: The minimum is below zero, so a low-quality pawn can lose up to {0} levels in a skill on their birthday.
LanguageData.VP_Section_TraitsTip: When off, this profile leaves vanilla trait generation untouched.
LanguageData.VP_CountProtectedTraits: Count xenotype/forced traits toward the trait count
LanguageData.VP_CountProtectedTraitsTip: When off, the range below counts only traits this mod rolls, and traits forced by a xenotype, gene, backstory or scenario are added on top. When on, the range counts every trait the pawn has. Forced traits are never removed either way.
LanguageData.VP_TraitCountTipTotal: Total traits on the pawn, including xenotype and forced traits.
LanguageData.VP_TraitCountTipRolled: Traits this mod rolls. Xenotype, gene, backstory and scenario traits are added on top.
LanguageData.VP_TraitCountTipBody: A HARD LIMIT, unlike Skill shift and Passion budget. Quality picks a point between the handles and the roll never leaves them. There is no trait spread setting.\n\nMore traits is not better. Traits are picked without regard to quality, so a wider range only buys more draws from the same pool, including the ones that cause mental breaks. Vanilla's own range is 2 to 3.
LanguageData.VP_Section_PassionsTip: When off, this profile leaves vanilla passion assignment untouched.
LanguageData.VP_PassionSpreadTip:
How much the total passion budget varies between pawns, in pips (a Minor passion costs 1, a Major costs 1.5). This is the typical spread, not the maximum; the line below shows the extreme.

The opposite of Skill spread: this varies one budget per pawn, so it makes pawns differ from each other rather than making one pawn uneven.

It is added on top of Passion budget, so a high value can push a pawn past either handle of that range.
LanguageData.VP_MajorBiasTip: How often the budget is spent on a Major passion instead of a Minor one. Majors always go to the pawn's best skills first.
LanguageData.VP_PassionBudgetTip:
Points spent on passions. A Minor passion costs 1, a Major costs 1.5. Presets use fractional budgets, so this reads to one decimal.

A TARGET, NOT A LIMIT. Quality picks one point between the handles: the low handle is what the lowest-quality pawn aims for, the high handle the highest. Passion spread then varies each pawn around that point, and can carry them past either handle.

A pawn has 12 skills and each holds at most one passion, so {0} is the most a budget can buy: every skill Major. Reaching it needs Major bias at maximum, and at lower bias the budget runs out of skills sooner.
LanguageData.VP_PassionCaptionTargets: Targets, not limits. Passion spread can carry a pawn outside them, and every pawn still gets at least one passion.
LanguageData.VP_PassionCaptionZero: Minimum is 0, so pawns with no passions are possible.
LanguageData.VP_ActiveColonyProfileCaption: Default profile for player colonists and neutral pawns:
LanguageData.VP_OverridesBeatThis: Overrides on a pawn's faction, race or xenotype take precedence over this.
LanguageData.VP_GeneralCaption: These apply to every profile and are not changed by switching profiles.
LanguageData.VP_HostileToggleTip: When off, raiders and other hostile pawns are generated exactly as in vanilla and this mod never touches them. When on, they are generated from the profile you pick below.
LanguageData.VP_HostileProfileCaption: Profile used for raiders and other hostiles:
LanguageData.VP_HostileProfileTip: Colonists are selected by the player, but raiders arrive directly. A separate hostile profile balances raider difficulty independently from your colony.
LanguageData.VP_GrowUpToggle: Apply variance to children growing up
LanguageData.VP_GrowUpToggleTip: Applies trait and passion variance when a child turns 13. The mod waits for growth choices to resolve, then tops up traits and passions to match profile targets. Existing traits and passions are never removed.
LanguageData.VP_VerboseLoggingTip: Rethrows exceptions instead of swallowing them, and logs a per-pawn breakdown of how traits and passions were assigned. Leave off for normal play.
LanguageData.VP_Confirm_ResetAll: Reset all settings to defaults? Every custom profile, override and option will be restored.
LanguageData.VP_ShareTip: Copies your whole configuration to the clipboard as text: every custom profile, both override lists with their priorities, and the options above. Paste it anywhere to share, or import someone else's.
LanguageData.VP_Msg_Exported: Varied Pawns settings copied to the clipboard.
LanguageData.VP_Msg_ExportFailed: Could not export settings. See the log for details.
LanguageData.VP_Confirm_Import: Importing replaces ALL of your Varied Pawns settings: every custom profile, both override lists, and the general options.\n\nThis cannot be undone. Continue?
LanguageData.VP_EnableOverridesTip: When enabled, specific faction, race and xenotype profiles take precedence over the Hostile and General profiles.
LanguageData.VP_EnableOverridesHint: Enable the checkbox above to configure per-faction, per-race and per-xenotype profiles.
LanguageData.VP_FactionPrecedence: Faction Overrides Take Priority Over Race & Xenotype Overrides
LanguageData.VP_FactionPrecedenceTip: When checked, a pawn matching a Faction override and also a Race or Xenotype override at the same priority (an Empire Neanderthal, say) uses the Faction override. When unchecked, Race and Xenotype win.\n\nRace always beats Xenotype at equal priority, whatever this is set to.
LanguageData.VP_PriorityTip:
Every override defaults to Normal. Higher priorities win over lower ones.

At equal priority the order is Faction, then Race, then Xenotype, or Race, Xenotype, then Faction if the faction-precedence toggle above is off.

Anything not listed here has no override and falls back to the hostile or colony profile.
LanguageData.VP_Confirm_DeleteAllFactionOverrides: Delete all faction overrides? Every custom faction assignment will be cleared.
LanguageData.VP_Confirm_RestoreFactionOverrides: Restore default faction overrides? Every faction assignment goes back to its shipped default.
LanguageData.VP_Confirm_DeleteAllXenotypeOverrides: Delete all xenotype overrides? Every custom xenotype assignment will be cleared.
LanguageData.VP_Confirm_RestoreXenotypeOverrides: Restore default xenotype overrides? Every xenotype assignment goes back to its shipped default.
LanguageData.VP_NoRaceOverrides: No race overrides configured. None ship by default, because the races available depend on which race mods you have installed.
LanguageData.VP_Confirm_DeleteAllRaceOverrides: Delete all race overrides? Every custom race assignment will be cleared.
